SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient: Logan Notreal, 69-year-old female.
HPI: Patient reports onset of low back pain on 07/24/2026. She describes constant aching pain in the lumbar region without radiation. She reports new-onset saddle anesthesia. She also notes recent onset of bladder dysfunction. She denies fever, weight loss, or trauma.
ROS: otherwise negative.
Vital signs: stable.
General: well-appearing but in mild discomfort.
Spine: tenderness over lumbar paraspinals, range of motion limited due to pain.
Neuro: Strength 5/5 bilaterally in upper extremities; lower extremity strength 5/5 hip flexion, 4/5 knee extension, 4/5 ankle dorsiflexion; right ankle jerk is 1+ (hypoactive). Sensation decreased in saddle area. Rectal tone reduced.
Assessment: Low back pain (\"M54.50\") with concerning features for possible cauda equina syndrome given saddle anesthesia and bladder dysfunction.
Plan: Continue close monitoring; advise patient to return immediately for worsening symptoms; no conservative treatment has been initiated; obtain urgent lumbar MRI to rule out cauda equina syndrome.
